correctness.rationale: Every projective binary [n,k] code corresponds to one rank-full subset of F2^k without zero. Exhaustion under generating transvections checks all rank-full GL(k,2) orbits k<=4 (1,2,6,36) and no identical sorted spectra. All dimension-five rank-full codes with <=7 columns normalize to I5 and <=2 extras: 1+26+325 exact cases and canonical representatives reveal 1,4,8 distinct and unique spectra. Higher k at length <=7 has codimension <=1 and is determined by the MacWilliams dual enumerator. The two explicit [8,5,2] generators have enumerator 1+3z²+8z³+7z⁴+8z⁵+5z⁶ but their three weight-two words span ranks 2 and 3. Each invertible map must increase at least one weight 2 to >=3 and decrease at least one weight >=3 to 2, yielding distortion >=9/4. The explicit independent image basis (1,4,7,8,20) realizes all 31 weight ratios in [2/3,3/2], proving equality. Standalone checker recomputed all finite certificates without approximate numerics.

originality.rationale: Bouyukliev (2006) already enumerates all projective binary code classes to dimension six, including the relevant class counts, but its inspected published counts by minimum distance and automorphism order do not imply injectivity/collision of the full Hamming spectra or exact linear code distortion without a new comparison. Bennett, Fox and Morrell (arXiv:2607.26261, 2026) give the distortion definition and complexity results, not this first projective isospectral boundary or 9/4 witness. Ding (2020) gives the Boolean Walsh correspondence, not a first-collision classification. Related research records address quinary isospectral codes or unrelated projective comparisons, not this binary [8,5] theorem. Novelty is best-knowledge only and is at risk from the complete earlier catalogue or older spectral-classification tables.

value.rationale: A natural obstruction question for Hamming-spectrum-only code comparison is settled at the first possible projective dimension and blocklength, together with an exact best linear distortion for a concrete shortest pair. The sharp dimension and length barriers come from global complete finite classifications rather than arbitrary parameter slices. The span-rank obstruction is a structural invariant invisible to an ordinary weight enumerator and is operationally related to the recently formulated code-distortion problem. Preexisting projective class counts are acknowledged, and no novel minimum distance or coding-rate gains are asserted.
